newsitem.title: HUNGARY: U.S.'s MMI to bid for Hungarian radio franchise.
newsitem.headline: U.S.'s MMI to bid for Hungarian radio franchise.

text.p: U.S.-based Metromedia International (MMI) said on Wednesday it planned to bid for one or more Hungarian national commercial radio franchises, the company announced on Wednesday.

"We are currently putting together a consortium to bid for the franchises," president and CEO Carl Brazell of MMI, a subsidiary of Atlanta-based Metromedia International Group , told reporters, adding that the consortium could bid for "one or both" of the two national FM frequencies available.

Brazell declined to name other partners in the consortium but added they did not include other radio companies. Hungarian regulations require that 25 percent plus one vote of the consortium should be Hungarian-owned.

In the tender invited by the National Radio and Television Board (ORTT), the minimum price for each franchise has been set at three billion forints plus 25 percent VAT, a figure which several potential bidders have described as unreasonably high.
Brazell said the minimum price would make bidding difficult but MMI would certainly be in a position to meet it.
"The ORTT has set a very high price and going far above that would be stretching things," he said. "We are certainly capable of financing it from our own resources"
He added that the final bid will be a mix between as high a bid as possible and a high quality of programming.
MMI has been present on the Hungarian radio market for four years through its ownership of Juventus Radio, which accounts for 49 percent of the country's total listenership.
MMI also operates radio stations in the Czech Republic, Russia, Latvia and Estonia.
Bids for the Hungarian tender are to be submitted on September 8.
Metromedia International Group includes Goldwyn Entertainment Company, the Motion Picture Corporation of America (MPCA) and Orion studios.
